clue.text: Lots of people at the Spanish railway pub

parts.note: a host is a great number, a multitude
el is Spanish for 'the'

explanation.surface: A crowd gathers at a Spanish railway bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostelry is an old-fashioned or jocular word for an inn or tavern.

clue.text: Temporary difficulty heading off causes discomfort

indicators.note: the head of the word, its first letter, is taken off

parts.note: a hitch is a temporary snag or setback

explanation.surface: A short-lived problem that sets out causes trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is an irritating sensation on the skin, a mild physical unease.

clue.text: Criticise roofing material

definitions.meaning: to attack harshly in a review
thin grey stone tiles used on roofs

explanation.surface: Complaining about what a roof is made of.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense means to pan or censure; the noun is the split stone laid as roof tiles.

clue.text: Practical approach is covered by field of study

indicators.note: one piece is wrapped round, covered by, the other

parts.note: a realm is a domain or sphere of knowledge

explanation.surface: A pragmatic attitude belongs within some academic discipline.
explanation.definitionFit: Realism is the attitude of facing facts and dealing with situations pragmatically.

clue.text: Bright and popular, instruct man to include electric current

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular

indicators.note: the two words around are made to take in another letter

parts.note: to tell someone to do something is to instruct them
a gent is a gentleman, a man
I is the symbol for electric current in physics

explanation.surface: A clever, well-liked person is told to bring in some electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: Bright is used of a person with a quick, clever mind.

clue.text: After pressure athlete recalled early race

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure

indicators.note: called back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a miler is a runner who races over a mile

explanation.surface: Under pressure, a runner remembers an earlier race.
explanation.definitionFit: A prelim is a preliminary heat run before the final rounds.

clue.text: Present gift to disheartened Brownie Pack?

indicators.note: having the heart, the middle letters, removed leaves only the outside letters

parts.note: to stow is to pack away

explanation.surface: A present is given to a downcast Brownie troop.
explanation.walkthrough: A Brownie is a junior Girl Guide; 'Pack' looks like her troop but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestow is to confer or give something as an honour or gift.

clue.text: It's descriptive of army test reformed rioter participates in

indicators.note: the jumbled letters take part inside the other word

parts.note: a trial is a test

indicators.note: the letters are formed anew, rearranged

explanation.surface: A test that a reformed rioter takes part in, perhaps for the army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformed' and 'participates in' work together; the Territorial Army is Britain's volunteer reserve force, so 'It's' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective names the British reserve force, the Territorial Army.

clue.text: Lord's action? One of four maybe

definitions.meaning: Lord's is the London cricket ground, where the action is batting turns
a Test match has four turns at batting, two per side

explanation.surface: A query about what a nobleman did, one of four.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's, with its apostrophe, is the famous cricket ground in London, not a peer.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a side's turn at batting is this; a full Test has four of them.

clue.text: Move in specified direction from place of bliss (endless)

indicators.note: the last letter is cut off

parts.note: heaven is the abode of bliss

explanation.surface: Travelling a set way away from paradise, without end.
explanation.definitionFit: In sailing, a vessel will heave ahead or heave to, moving in a stated direction.

clue.text: Difficult situation as moderates suffer setback

indicators.note: being set back, the word is turned round

parts.note: wets are moderate Conservatives, a British political term

explanation.surface: Trouble brews when the moderates lose ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Wets were the moderate Tories opposed to Thatcher's hard line.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a stew is to be in a state of anxious trouble.

clue.text: Financial stake in Slainte restaurant

indicators.note: the letters sit in the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone owns a share in a restaurant called Slainte.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a share or money invested in a business is having this in it.

clue.text: Guy's singular sound of disapproval

parts.note: belonging to a guy, a man: his
S is the grammar abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A man's unique way of booing.
explanation.definitionFit: Audiences make this sibilant noise to show scorn or disapproval.

clue.text: Reportedly watch team — Blackpool?

indicators.note: as heard, the words are matched by their sound

parts.note: to see a side is to watch a team

explanation.surface: A fan is said to watch a football team from Blackpool.
explanation.walkthrough: Blackpool is an English resort town on the Lancashire coast, and also a football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackpool is an example of a coastal holiday resort, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Nice article moved tradesman

indicators.note: the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A pleasant newspaper piece shifted a workman.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who installs and repairs wiring is one example.

clue.text: Seldom is artist meeting bank

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
to bank on something is to rely on it

explanation.surface: An artist rarely meets a riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean not often, infrequently.

clue.text: After time, procedure is hackneyed

indicators.note: the second piece follows the first

parts.note: a rite is a ceremonial procedure

explanation.surface: Over time, the routine becomes stale.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe a remark worn out from overuse, stale.

clue.text: House police have as starting point

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police
to own is to have

explanation.surface: The police take a house as their base.
explanation.definitionFit: The town someone comes from is where their life started, their point of origin.

clue.text: Hymn or hit newly associated with web media

indicators.note: the letters are made anew, rearranged

explanation.surface: A hymn becomes a fresh hit through online media.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a well-known Christian hymn, sung at funerals and the FA Cup Final.

clue.text: Quiet street with ambience in America at higher level

indicators.note: the pieces go in the abbreviation for the country

parts.note: US is the United States
P is piano, quietly, in music
an air is an atmosphere or ambience

explanation.surface: A calm street with atmosphere in America sits higher up.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on an upper floor of a building is being higher up.

clue.text: Raising crops up to specific period

parts.note: till means until, up to
an age is a particular era

explanation.surface: Farming continues until a set period.
explanation.definitionFit: This is cultivation of land, preparing and working it to grow crops.

clue.text: Relative needs money to keep us

indicators.note: the outer word keeps, holds, the other within

parts.note: a coin is a piece of money

explanation.surface: A family member needs cash to support us.
explanation.definitionFit: A child of one's uncle or aunt is a family relation.

clue.text: Large stove used in mountains

definitions.meaning: a big kitchen cooker with several hobs and ovens

explanation.surface: A big cooker used up in the hills.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen range is a big cooker; a mountain range is a line of peaks.

clue.text: Deposited port

definitions.meaning: past tense of leave, set down and went
port is the ...-hand side of a ship

explanation.definitionFit: Something set down was left behind; port is the nautical word for the left side.
